key_insight: TRACE tackles long-horizon agent training by assigning rewards at the turn level instead of only at the final outcome. This lets the model credit useful intermediate actions even when the overall rollout fails.
problem_solved: The paper addresses credit assignment in multi-turn AI agents that use many tool calls before answering. Outcome-only rewards become sparse, noisy, and misleading over long trajectories, making it hard to learn which actions actually helped.
method: Estimate credit for each turn in a trajectory, rather than relying only on end-of-episode success or failure.
Use turn-level reward assignment to identify and reinforce helpful intermediate actions in long tool-use sequences.
Improve post-training signal quality for agents operating over tens or hundreds of interactions.
impact: This makes training more stable and informative for long-horizon agents, especially in tool-using and multi-step reasoning settings. Practitioners can expect better learning from partial progress instead of wasting signal from useful but failed trajectories.

paper_title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
paper_authors: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng
